records.title_en: Finance Minister András Kármán sets out planned cuts to state operating costs in the 2027 draft budget
records.summary_en:
Telex reports that Finance Minister András Kármán presented the 2027 draft budget at a government briefing on 20 October, continuing the explanation round that began the day before with Prime Minister Péter Magyar's speech in parliament. The draft sets a primary balance of -1.1% of GDP, interest costs of 3.8% and an ESA deficit of 4.9% (5.2% on a cash basis), with growth of 2.4%, inflation of 3% and public debt falling from 75.5% to 75.2% of GDP.

This is a draft budget being presented, not an adopted law; the report notes that some key figures, such as VAT revenue, are not yet known.

records.title_en: Polish lower house passes two bills liberalising abortion rules
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that the Sejm passed two bills on Tuesday 20 October: one would again allow abortion when a severe foetal abnormality is diagnosed, reversing the effect of a 2020 Constitutional Tribunal ruling (233 to 203); the other would decriminalise helping a woman obtain an unlawful abortion, currently punishable by up to three years in prison (217 to 213). Both bills go to the Senate and then to President Karol Nawrocki, who can sign, veto or refer them to the Constitutional Tribunal; the report considers a veto very likely.

This is a lower-house vote, not a law in force; the record does not assess the positions involved.

records.title_en: Chancellor Merz receives President Pavel in Berlin for talks on Czech-German relations and security
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International reports that German Chancellor Friedrich Merz received Czech President Petr Pavel, on a two-day working visit, at the Chancellery in Berlin for closed-door talks on bilateral relations, foreign policy and security. Pavel joined a round table of the German Council on Foreign Relations that evening and was due to speak at the Berlin Global Dialogue on Thursday.

The report records talks only; it mentions no agreement signed or decision taken.

records.title_en: Fourth unit of the Mochovce nuclear power plant begins supplying electricity to the grid
records.summary_en:
TASR reports that the operator Slovenské elektrárne (SE) says the fourth unit at Mochovce has begun supplying its first megawatt-hours after its grid connection on 15 October and is running at about 19% of capacity; physical start-up tests are complete and power start-up tests are under way. Trial operation still needs approval from the Nuclear Regulatory Authority (ÚJD), and SE expects full capacity next year.

This is first grid connection and initial supply, not commercial operation; the record draws no conclusion about prices or supply.

records.title_en: V4 economy ministers sign joint declaration on EU energy priorities and seek talks on EU funding for industry
records.summary_en:
TASR reports that on 19 October in Bratislava the V4 ministers and EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen signed a joint declaration on EU energy priorities. Slovak Economy Minister Denisa Saková said the V4 want EU funds, through cohesion policy or more flexibility in the Modernisation Fund, to help industry with high energy prices as a temporary measure, want EU competitiveness support to cover operating costs, and want nuclear power treated on a par with renewables.

The declaration states positions; the funding and nuclear requests are positions for discussion with the Commission, and the report mentions no EU decision.

records.title_en: Slovak Constitutional Court rules the cooperating-defendants part of the criminal procedure amendment unconstitutional
records.summary_en:
TASR reports that on 21 October the Constitutional Court ruled unconstitutional the part of the amendment to the Code of Criminal Procedure, passed by fast-track procedure last December, that concerns so-called cooperating defendants; the amendment had been challenged by 51 opposition MPs, Prosecutor-General Maroš Žilinka and the Specialised Criminal Court, and the court rejected the petitions on the remaining parts.

This is a court ruling; the report does not state its direct consequences for individual cases, and the record infers none.

records.title_en: Germany's tobacco tax act enters into force early because of a technical error
records.summary_en:
ZDFheute reports that the new Tobacco Tax Act was published in the Federal Law Gazette on Tuesday and, because of a 'technical error' in its entry-into-force date, took effect the next day although it was meant to apply from 2027; the Federal Finance Ministry says a correction is under way. As the required tax stamps are not yet available, manufacturers cannot pay the higher duties and prices are expected to stay unchanged for now; the ministry projects a 20-pack rising from €8.77 in 2027 to €11.36 in 2030.

This is a procedural error in publication and entry into force; the record draws no fiscal or consumer conclusions.

records.title_en: Romanian parliament approves the Niculescu cabinet
records.summary_en:
Radio Romania International reports that parliament approved the cabinet of independent Prime Minister Luca Niculescu by 280 votes to 58 (233 required), with PSD, PNL, UDMR, the national minorities group and smaller groups in favour and AUR and USR against. Two-thirds of the ministries went to PSD members and the rest to non-affiliated experts endorsed by President Nicușor Dan; Niculescu named a budget adjustment, the 2027 budget and energy security as priorities and said the deficit target is not negotiable.

This is a parliamentary confidence vote; the record does not assess the cabinet or infer the effects of its programme.

records.title_en: Eurostat data: Romania had the EU's largest budget deficit in 2025
records.summary_en:
Radio Romania International reports that Eurostat data published on Wednesday 21 October show Romania's government deficit narrowing to 7.8% of GDP in 2025 (9.2% in 2024, 6.6% in 2023), still the EU's highest, ahead of Poland, Belgium and France; the EU average was 3.1% and the euro area 3%, 11 member states were at or above 3%, and Cyprus, Denmark, Greece and Portugal posted surpluses.

This reports an official statistical release; the record adds no debt figure the report does not give and makes no forecast.

records.title_en: European Parliament responds to Brnabić's protest over its observation mission to Serbia
records.summary_en:
N1 reports that the European Parliament replied to a formal protest by Serbian parliament speaker and acting president Ana Brnabić about its observation delegation for the 25 October elections; she objected in particular to MEP Andreas Schieder leading the seven-member delegation. The Parliament said the mission will follow international observation methodology and remain independent and impartial; Schieder said he will present its findings at a press conference on 26 October.

This is a formal institutional exchange; the record does not assess the electoral process or predict the result.

records.title_en: Croatian government's 216th session sends the final Hospitality Act to parliament and sets the annual pension supplement
records.summary_en:
The Croatian government website reports that at its 216th session on 21 October the government sent the final proposal of the Hospitality Act to parliament for second reading: it digitises procedures through the e-turizam system, requires a registration number for accommodation advertised online, extends inspection powers to customs and municipal wardens, raises fines for unregistered activity and extends temporary permits for private renters to 31 December 2030. The session also set the 2026 annual pension supplement at €7 per year of service (€208 on average, about €260 million paid in December), adopted two railway action plans (estimated €603 million and €407.2 million) and sent a law on the resolution of insurance and reinsurance companies, with Hanfa as resolution authority, to parliament.

Sending a bill to parliament is not its adoption; the record lists the session decisions only and infers no effects.

records.title_en: EU Court of Justice rules Czech law breaches the right to a lawyer during police questioning
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International reports that the Court of Justice of the EU ruled on Thursday 22 October that Czech law breaches EU rules by allowing suspects to be questioned without a lawyer if defence counsel does not arrive within 48 hours of arrest; the court upheld the European Commission's complaint and found a similar breach in Hungary, where the limit is two hours. Czechia was not fined, but the Commission can seek financial penalties if the ruling is not complied with.

This is a ruling in infringement proceedings; the record infers no legislative follow-up.

records.title_en: Polish and Indian prime ministers meet in New Delhi and set a goal of doubling trade by 2030
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Prime Minister Narendra Modi met in New Delhi on 22 October, the first visit to India by a Polish prime minister in 16 years. They set a shared goal of doubling bilateral trade by 2030 and agreed to expand cooperation in mining, shipbuilding, energy, space, defence technologies and startups; the report puts bilateral trade at just over $6 billion, with Polish goods exports to India of €1.4 billion and imports of €4.3 billion last year.

The report mentions no specific documents signed or investment commitments; the trade goal is a stated intention, not an outcome.

records.title_en: German tax estimate: higher revenue expected for the federal government, Länder and municipalities
records.summary_en:
ZDFheute reports that the tax estimate working group at the Federal Finance Ministry published its results on 22 October: federal, Länder and municipal revenue is expected to be about €11 billion a year higher on average through 2030 than previously forecast, including €10.9 billion more in 2027; 2026 revenue is expected at €997.9 billion, roughly in line with May, and 2027 at about €1,044 billion. Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said there is no new room for 2027 and warned against spending the extra revenue in advance.

This is an official revenue forecast, not a budget decision; the record infers no fiscal-policy consequences.

records.title_en: Croatian foreign ministry advises citizens to postpone non-essential travel to Serbia ahead of the elections
records.summary_en:
N1 reports that Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs advised citizens to avoid non-essential travel to Serbia and to take extra care if they must go, citing possible political tensions around the 25 October parliamentary elections and past incidents involving Serbian authorities' conduct towards Croatian citizens; it urged them to avoid protests, rallies and large gatherings and noted they can contact the Croatian embassy in Serbia.

This is a government travel advisory; the record does not assess bilateral relations or predict the electoral situation.

records.title_en: Czech lower house approves the key parameters of the 2027 state budget with a CZK 386 billion deficit
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International reports that the lower house approved the main parameters of the draft 2027 state budget with the governing coalition in favour, after opposition proposals to return the draft to the government for a smaller deficit failed. The deficit is planned to rise from CZK 310 billion this year to CZK 386 billion next year, mainly financed by more state debt; revenue rises by CZK 80.8 billion to CZK 2.199 trillion and expenditure by CZK 156.8 billion to CZK 2.585 trillion. MPs can no longer change the main parameters and will now debate individual chapters and reallocations.

This is an intermediate vote; the budget is not yet adopted, the report gives no vote count, and the record infers no fiscal effects.

records.title_en: Preliminary count: Student List leads Serbia's parliamentary election, Election Commission says
records.summary_en:
N1 reports that on the morning of 26 October Serbia's Republic Election Commission (RIK) announced that, with 8,077 of 8,392 polling stations processed, the Student List had 52.54% of the vote in the 25 October snap parliamentary election, the SNS-led United Serbia coalition 39.29% and the SPS list 2.18%. RIK put final turnout at 68.78%, with 1.29% invalid ballots.

These are preliminary results, not certified final results; the seat figures in the report (140 for the Student List, 103 for United Serbia) are CeSID projections, not an official allocation.

records.title_en: International observers cite serious shortcomings in Serbia's parliamentary elections
records.summary_en:
N1 reports that on 26 October the OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights, the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe and the European Parliament delegation issued a preliminary statement on Serbia's 25 October snap parliamentary election. They noted high turnout and strong competition, but a deeply polarised atmosphere and unequal campaign conditions in which the ruling party benefited from entrenched advantages, including misuse of public resources. Preparations and candidate registration were described as generally efficient, but concerns were raised about the Election Commission's impartiality, complaint handling and trust in the voter register; 60% of the 1,485 polling stations observed lacked independent access for voters with disabilities.

This is the missions' preliminary assessment, not a ruling by a court or electoral body; items such as digital surveillance are concerns reported by the missions.

records.title_en: Serbia's average net salary in August at roughly 1,000 euros
records.summary_en:
N1, citing figures released by the Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia (RZS) on 26 October, reports that the average gross salary in August 2026 was about €1,385 (RSD 161,953), the average net salary about €1,000 and the median net salary about €800. The average net salary rose 11.1% year on year in nominal terms and 8.7% in real terms; in January–August net salaries were up 11.4% nominally and 8.5% in real terms.

The euro amounts are conversions given in the report; nominal and real growth are different measures, and no cause of the wage change is inferred here.

records.title_en: Serbia's Anti-Corruption Agency finds SNS broke campaign-finance rules
records.summary_en:
N1 reports that in a decision of 26 October Serbia's Anti-Corruption Agency found that the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) broke the Law on the Financing of Political Activities during the campaign for the 25 October parliamentary election: promotional materials handed out at its stands in Vrnjačka Banja and 25 other cities did not carry the legally required producer information on each item. The case followed a complaint filed on 16 October; the agency ruled that the information must appear on every item, not only on the packaging.

The report mentions no sanction or next step; the SNS view that information on the packaging was sufficient is the party's position.

records.title_en: Serbian oil company NIS receives a new US operating licence
records.summary_en:
N1 reports that Serbia's oil company NIS said it received a new special licence from the US Treasury on 30 October allowing it to keep operating until 11 December 2026. The licence covers the business, contracts and agreements of NIS and its operating subsidiaries, including refinery processing, crude imports, security-of-supply transactions, technical maintenance and financial settlements.

The licence details come from the company's statement; the report does not reproduce the licence itself. It is a time-limited licence, not a lifting of sanctions.

records.title_en: Serbia's central bank revokes the licence of Alta Banka
records.summary_en:
N1 reports that the Executive Board of the National Bank of Serbia revoked the operating licence of Alta Banka a.d. Beograd, saying its supervisory measures to strengthen the bank's liquidity had not worked, its financial condition had "deteriorated significantly" and depositors were at risk, citing the Law on Banks. Following a court ruling, the Deposit Insurance Agency will be appointed bankruptcy trustee; insured deposits up to €50,000 will be paid out, and card operations, domestic and foreign settlements and branches were suspended immediately.

The revocation is a supervisory decision; reports about the owner's political ties and state contracts are media reporting and are not established here.

records.title_en: Serbia's Election Commission announces final parliamentary election results
records.summary_en:
N1 reports that on 5 November Serbia's Republic Election Commission announced the final results of the 25 October snap parliamentary election: the "Student List – Students Win" received 2,354,417 votes and 140 seats, and the "United Serbia – Aleksandar Vučić" list 1,731,323 votes and 103 seats; the remaining seven seats went to five minority lists. There were 6,451,292 registered voters, 4,444,310 voted and 4,385,065 ballots were valid.

These are the commission's final results; constituting parliament and electing a government are later steps, and no outcome of government formation is inferred.

records.title_en: Serbia's new parliament to hold its opening session on 17 November
records.summary_en:
N1 reports that on 8 November Acting President Ana Brnabić announced that the newly elected National Assembly will hold its inaugural session on 17 November at 10 a.m.; it will verify mandates and elect a speaker, deputy speakers and a secretary-general, chaired by the oldest member until a speaker is chosen. The Election Commission adopted its final report on 5 November and its mandates report on 6 November; the outgoing government stays in office until a new one is formed, and parliament has up to 90 days after it is constituted to elect a government.

This announces a session date; the session has not yet taken place, and nothing is inferred about the composition or programme of a new government.

records.title_en: Croatia's JANAF suspends crude deliveries to Serbia after a pipeline accident
records.summary_en:
N1 reports that Croatia's JANAF confirmed it has suspended crude oil transport to Serbia's Pančevo refinery since 6 November after an accident during maintenance on the Sisak–Slavonski Brod section, with an estimated 500,000 litres of crude spilled; JANAF says all the spilled oil was collected and returned to the system and that repairs and cleanup are under way. Serbia's NIS says it has sufficient reserves, refinery throughput is unaffected and the domestic market is adequately supplied.

No date for resuming deliveries has been given; the spill volume is an estimate, and the statements on reserves and supply are the companies' own.

records.title_en: Australia's MDI takes over the Majdanpek exploration project once funded by Rio Tinto
records.summary_en:
N1, citing an ASX announcement, reports that Australian miner Raiden Resources completed the sale of its Majdanpek West exploration project to Middle Island Resources (MDI) after Serbia's Ministry of Mining and Energy renewed the exploration licence in late September. MDI pays AU$300,000 in cash or shares and the seller keeps a 1% net smelter return royalty; the project lies about 3 km from the copper-gold mine run by Zijin Mining at Majdanpek, where Rio Tinto had planned to spend $40 million on early exploration from 2018 before withdrawing.

This is a transaction in an exploration project, not a mining permit or a production decision; geological results and investment figures are company disclosures.

records.title_en: Croatia has spent €5.3 billion on post-earthquake reconstruction so far
records.summary_en:
The Croatian government website reports that on 27 October, at the opening of three fully reconstructed buildings in Zagreb, Prime Minister Andrej Plenković said the government has so far spent €5.3 billion on post-earthquake reconstruction, about €3.15 billion for the Zagreb earthquake and €2.15 billion for the Petrinja earthquake. Funding came from about €1 billion from the EU Solidarity Fund, about €2 billion from the National Recovery and Resilience Plan and about €1 billion a year from the state budget. The three buildings are worth €100 million.

The amounts are the government's own figures; the prime minister's statement that the whole reconstruction will be finished in three to four years is an expectation, not a settled outcome.

records.title_en: Croatia sets the 2027 minimum wage at €1,130 gross
records.summary_en:
The Croatian government website reports that on 29 October Prime Minister Andrej Plenković announced at the opening of a government session that, after consultations, the government decided to raise the gross minimum wage for 2027 from €1,050 to €1,130, an increase of €80 or 7.6%; the minimum student hourly wage, which is linked to it, rises from €6.56 to €7.06. The government will also continue to cover, through the Croatian Employment Service, the difference between the old and new minimum wage for applying employers in the first three months of 2027.

The page does not give the publication date of the formal regulation; figures such as about 50,000 workers on the minimum wage are the prime minister's statements.

records.title_en: Croatia presents Labour Act amendments on pay transparency
records.summary_en:
The Croatian government website reports that on 2 November the Ministry of Labour presented draft amendments to the Labour Act implementing the EU Pay Transparency Directive and the Platform Work Directive and aligning annual leave rules with EU Court of Justice rulings. Under the draft, job applicants must be told the starting salary or range before or during the interview, employees may request average pay for comparable jobs broken down by sex, and employers with more than 100 staff must report pay data, generated automatically by a National Pay Transparency System run by Fina.

The draft is in public consultation on e-Savjetovanja and has not been adopted; employers would get at least six months to adapt after entry into force.

records.title_en: Croatia's first estimate puts October inflation at 4.9%; finance minister pledges continued energy-price protection
records.summary_en:
The Croatian government website reports that the State Statistics Office's first estimate put October inflation at 4.9% year on year, with energy up 20.7% and food, drink and tobacco up 0.2%. On 4 November Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Tomislav Ćorić said the government would keep protecting citizens and the economy from excessive energy price rises; in public-sector pay talks the government offered a cumulative 3-percentage-point rise in the base from 2027 plus a new meal allowance, which the unions rejected, with talks to resume next week.

The inflation figure is a first estimate; the protection pledge is a statement and the pay offer a negotiating position, while an average 2026 inflation rate of 4.5% is the minister's projection.

records.title_en: Croatian government extends the household heating price subsidy
records.summary_en:
The Croatian government website reports that at its 222nd session on 5 November the government, as part of its 11th aid package, extended the decision subsidising heat prices for households from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027 for all end customers except those using heat mainly for business. For central heating the subsidy equals the difference between the end price on 1 October and on 30 September 2026; for closed and standalone systems it is based on the rise in procurement costs compared with the previous heating season, with unit amounts set by the regulator HERA and payments made by the Ministry of Economy.

The page gives no total cost; protecting citizens from rising energy costs is the policy aim, not a measured effect.

records.title_en: Croatia signs nearly €275 million in water contracts and €4.5 million for Roma-area infrastructure
records.summary_en:
The Croatian government website reports that after the government session on 5 November two contract-signing ceremonies worth almost €280 million in total were held at the National and University Library. About €275 million is for public water supply and wastewater projects: 22 contracts funded by the National Recovery and Resilience Plan cover over 116 km of water mains and almost 26 km of sewers in 13 counties, and a separate €213.9 million contract for water infrastructure on Vir is co-financed by the Competitiveness and Cohesion Programme. A further €4.5 million funds infrastructure in areas inhabited by the Roma minority.

These are signed contracts, not completed projects; beneficiary numbers are the government's expectations.

records.title_en: Plenković and EU Commissioner Jørgensen discuss energy security and affordable housing
records.summary_en:
The Croatian government website reports that on 5 November Prime Minister Andrej Plenković met Dan Jørgensen, EU Commissioner for Energy and Housing, at Banski dvori to discuss energy security, affordability of energy prices, the energy transition and European affordable-housing initiatives. Plenković stressed the strategic importance of the Krk LNG terminal and gas pipeline investments, described the JANAF pipeline as a key route for non-Russian oil, and presented the government's caps on electricity, gas and fuel prices and the National Housing Policy Plan to 2030.

This was a meeting; the government website reports no signed agreement or decision.

records.title_en: Croatia lowers maximum retail fuel prices from 10 November
records.summary_en:
The Croatian government website reports that the government held a telephone session and adopted decrees continuing fuel price regulation for seven days from 10 November 2026. New maximum retail prices are €1.61 per litre for petrol (down €0.08), €1.85 for diesel (down €0.04) and €1.38 for blue diesel (down €0.07), and €1.81 per kg for LPG in tanks and €2.39 in bottles (both down €0.06); the caps are calculated from the base fossil fuel price of the previous seven days plus a capped premium.

The government says prices would be higher without the measures, which is its own calculation; nothing is inferred about future fuel prices.

records.title_en: Slovenian government's 17th session tightens the Foreigners Act and adopts a healthcare investment bill
records.summary_en:
The Slovenian government website reports that at its 17th regular session on 22 October the government adopted an amendment to the Foreigners Act raising the lawful-residence period required for family reunification from one to three years, increasing the general sufficient-means threshold for residence permits from €507.43 to €1,014.86 and raising Slovenian language requirements. It also adopted a bill providing €1.873 billion for healthcare investment in 2026–2036, replacing the 2021–2031 act, and an amendment reinstating the four-subject vocational matura.

These are government bills that still go to the National Assembly; the bill implementing the Pact on Migration and Asylum and others only had their texts determined.

records.title_en: Slovenia prices a $500 million 10-year bond at a 5.6% coupon
records.summary_en:
The Slovenian government website reports that on 27 October the Republic of Slovenia priced a US$500 million 10-year 144A/Reg S benchmark bond with a 5.600% coupon and a 5.630% reoffer yield, 65 basis points over US Treasuries; the order book exceeded US$785 million, with 65% from continental European investors and 27% from central banks and official institutions. The issue is fully swapped against USD/EUR exchange-rate risk, giving an effective cost of 4.124%, and funds the state budget.

This is the government's issuance notice; the page gives two different order-book totals, and the lower figure is used here.

records.title_en: Slovenian government sets the supplemented draft state budget for 2028
records.summary_en:
The Slovenian government website reports that at its 39th correspondence session on 29 October the government adopted the supplemented draft state budget for 2028 unchanged, rejecting the tabled amendments: revenue is projected at €17.7 billion and expenditure at €19.4 billion, with a deficit of up to €1.7 billion, about 2% of GDP. It also decided to intervene before the EU General Court in support of listing n-hexane as a substance of very high concern, and backed the draft EU common position on provisionally closing Chapter 22 with Montenegro.

This is a draft budget still to be adopted by the National Assembly; the deficit is a planned figure.

records.title_en: Slovenian, Austrian and Croatian foreign ministers meet in Vienna
records.summary_en:
The Slovenian government website reports that Foreign Minister Tone Kajzer attended the third trilateral meeting of the foreign ministers of Slovenia, Austria and Croatia in Vienna, covering EU enlargement to the Western Balkans, security and defence, migration, energy security and EU competitiveness; the ministers agreed on regular political dialogue and closer regional cooperation. He also held bilateral talks with Austria's Beate Meinl-Reisinger on the Slovenian minority in Austria, economic cooperation and the role of the Port of Koper.

No agreement was signed; the follow-up is continued dialogue at the C5 meeting in Budapest and a planned visit by the Austrian minister to Slovenia.

records.title_en: Slovenia's goods exports rise 13.9% year on year in September
records.summary_en:
The Statistical Office of Slovenia reported on 4 November that goods exports in September 2026 were €6.898 billion, up 13.9% year on year, and imports €6.500 billion, up 18.1%, for a surplus of €398 million; excluding processing operations, exports were €3.9 billion (+8.6%) and imports €4.0 billion (+9.8%). In January–September exports were €53.651 billion, down 2.8%, and imports €60.330 billion, up 14.3%, for a deficit of €6.680 billion.

Monthly 2026 data are provisional and may be revised; final data are due in June 2027.

records.title_en: Slovenian government opposes deputies' amendments to the healthcare investment financing act
records.summary_en:
The Slovenian government website reports that a group of deputies submitted to the National Assembly amendments to the act financing healthcare investment for 2021–2031 that would raise the additional annual funding commitments. On 4 November the government said it does not support the proposal because the increases are not sufficiently tied to project progress, implementation pace and medium-term public finance planning; it prefers its own new healthcare investment bill and related amendment, submitted to the National Assembly on 23 October, which fund investment to 2036.

This is the government's opinion on a deputies' bill, which the National Assembly will decide; the comparison of the two proposals is the government's assessment.

records.title_en: Slovenian government widens fuel aid for hauliers and sets up a rare-diseases fund
records.summary_en:
The Slovenian government website reports that at its 18th regular session on 5 November the government adopted amendments to the act on temporary measures against high fuel prices, letting road hauliers claim aid for diesel bought in other EU states covering up to 70% of the extra cost, capped at 20 cents per litre, with estimated sector aid rising from €29 million to €38 million. It also set up a public fund for advanced treatment of rare diseases with €10 million of earmarked capital, adopted Slovenia's draft position on the EU Cloud and AI Development Act, and backed proposals for consultative referendums on cutting bureaucracy and banning face coverings in public.

The referendum proposals were only supported, not called; the EU act position is a basis for further negotiation.

records.title_en: Slovenia welcomes the European Commission's 2026 enlargement package
records.summary_en:
The Slovenian government website reports that Slovenia welcomes the European Commission's 2026 enlargement package and stresses that progress must depend on meeting the accession criteria. Slovenia backs Montenegro concluding negotiations by the end of 2026 and signing an accession treaty next year, supports Moldova and Ukraine opening their remaining clusters, and expects Serbia to align with EU law; in the package the Commission assesses that Serbia has regressed on fundamental rights, rule of law and media freedom.

This is the Slovenian government's position; the country assessments come from the Commission's package, and no accession timetable is inferred.

records.title_en: Parent of Slovenia's Big Bang to acquire Serbian electronics retailer Gigatron
records.summary_en:
N1, citing a press release from investor Advance Capital Partners, reports that Bidigital Naložbe, parent of Slovenian electronics retailer Big Bang, is set to acquire 100% of Gigatron, Serbia's largest electronics and tech retailer; founder and CEO Vladan Janković would receive an equity stake in the Bidigital group and remain CEO. The combined group would have annual revenue above €550 million, more than 90 stores and over 1,700 employees in four countries.

The deal requires competition approval and has not closed; the price was not disclosed, and targets such as 2030 revenue are company figures.

records.title_en: Slovenia's industrial production up 2.1% year on year in September
records.summary_en:
The Statistical Office of Slovenia reported on 10 November that industrial production in September 2026 rose 0.3% month on month and 2.1% year on year, and 0.8% in the first three quarters; industrial turnover rose 0.5% on the month and 4.6% on the year (3.7% in January–September), and stocks rose 2.3% on the month and 4.6% on the year.

Data for the latest six months are provisional and may be revised when new data are published.

records.title_en: Leader of a junior coalition partner quits the Polish government
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that Katarzyna Pełczyńska-Nałęcz, leader of Poland 2050 and minister for funds and regional policy, resigned from the government and as party leader. Her decision followed a Sejm vote on 22 October in which a Polish People's Party bill abolishing two-term limits for mayors was defeated 213 to 215 after 15 coalition MPs voted with the opposition; Poland 2050 split on the vote. The party says it remains in the coalition, which keeps Prime Minister Donald Tusk's majority.

The resignation has taken place; nothing is inferred about the coalition's stability or the next election, and poll figures in the report are not used as evidence.

records.title_en: Poland and Vietnam announce a strategic partnership during Tusk's Hanoi visit
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited Hanoi and met Vietnam's prime minister, and the two countries upgraded ties to a strategic partnership covering trade and investment, security and defence, education, science and technology and cultural exchange; they committed to regular high-level contacts, fewer non-tariff barriers and deeper defence cooperation. It was the first visit by a Polish prime minister to Vietnam in 16 years; Poland runs a trade deficit with Vietnam.

Talks on Vietnamese purchases of Polish howitzers and armoured vehicles are ongoing, and plans such as LOT resuming direct flights are intentions, not signed contracts.

records.title_en: US chooses Poland to host a service facility for Patriot missiles
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that on 27 October the US Department of War announced it had chosen Poland to host a centre for servicing and maintaining PAC-3 missiles used in Patriot air defence systems, the first such facility outside the United States, ahead of bids from four other European countries. The choice was made by the US government with manufacturer Lockheed Martin; in 2025 Poland signed a $2 billion deal with the US for Patriot logistics support and training.

This is a site decision and the facility has not been built; the report gives no cost or opening date, and Polish officials' claims about the president's role are unverified.

records.title_en: Poland and the UK sign the Warsaw Defence Plan
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting signed the Warsaw Defence Plan with Poland during a visit to Warsaw; the British Ministry of Defence says it aims to "deter Russian threats". The plan builds on a strategic defence partnership signed earlier in 2026 and the Northolt Treaty signed in May, and covers joint development and production of next-generation air-defence missiles, drone and counter-drone technology, and Baltic Sea exercises and regional coordination.

The report gives no monetary amounts; the listed areas are the agreement's content and intentions, not delivered projects.

records.title_en: Poland approves its first fast-track renewable energy zones
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that the Wielkopolska regional assembly approved Poland's first plans for accelerated renewable energy development zones, covering about 105.4 hectares in four municipalities (Złotów, Lwówek, Rawicz and Słupca), where investors can build solar farms under simplified planning and environmental procedures, with an estimated technical potential of 66–80 MW. The legal basis is the EU's revised Renewable Energy Directive (RED III), under which the first zones were due by 21 February 2026.

These are regional planning decisions, not project approvals; the environment ministry's estimate of shorter permitting times is an estimate.

records.title_en: Standoff at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal over its chief justice
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that on the evening of 30 October a group of government-backed judges moved to take control of the Constitutional Tribunal from its chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, who is aligned with the opposition and President Karol Nawrocki: Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska said she had suspended him and his deputy under Article 130 of the law on common courts, and police surrounded the court and kept him from entering. The dispute stems from the government's refusal since 2023 to recognise the court over three unlawfully appointed judges; parliament elected eight new judges in 2026, but the president has refused to swear in five of them.

The two sides contest the legality of the actions and scholars question the legal basis for the suspension; no judgement on the legal dispute is made here.

records.title_en: Poland launches a security operation along the Kaliningrad border
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that Polish police launched a special operation to secure the area along the border with Russia's Kaliningrad exclave after receiving information that sabotage could occur there in the coming days, sending additional officers, including counter-terrorism units, to Podlasie and Warmia-Masuria and coordinating with the army, Border Guard and security services. National police chief Marek Boroń confirmed the operation, saying it was based partly on information from foreign security services.

The threat itself and its origin rest on unnamed sources, and police say the details are confidential; only the announced operation is recorded here.

records.title_en: Eurostat data: Poland has the EU's second-highest household electricity prices adjusted for purchasing power
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland, citing Eurostat data, reports that in the first half of 2026 Polish household electricity cost €29.99 per 100 kWh in nominal terms, the EU's seventh highest and above the EU average of €28.32, and 41.12 in purchasing power standards (PPS), second only to Romania's 46.89. In PPS terms Polish prices rose 10.7% from the second half of 2025; taxes and levies made up 39% of the final household price, the highest share in the EU.

Nominal and PPS-adjusted prices are different measures; views on coal costs and policy changes in the report belong to interviewees, and no causal claim is made here.

records.title_en: Chinese fashion platform Shein announces a €500 million investment in its Polish logistics hub
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that Shein announced a €500 million (2.2 billion zloty) investment to expand its logistics centre in Magnice near Wrocław, in operation since 2022. The company says the expansion will create about 2,000 jobs by the end of 2026, bringing employment at the site to around 10,000, with 6,500 autonomous sorting robots; the investment was presented by Leonard Lin, Shein's global head of public affairs.

This is an announced investment plan, not a signed agreement; the job figures come from local media, and faster delivery times are the company's claim.

records.title_en: S&P shifts Poland's credit outlook to negative and lowers its local-currency rating
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that S&P revised Poland's outlook to negative, describing its fiscal performance as "one of the most significant fiscal deteriorations globally", and lowered the long- and short-term local-currency ratings from A/A-1 to A-/A-2, in line with the foreign-currency ratings. The figures cited show a deficit of 7.3% of GDP in 2025, a forecast 6.7% for 2026 and 7.1% in the 2027 draft budget, far above the 3.7% required under the EU excessive deficit procedure; S&P expects net debt to exceed 70% of GDP by 2029.

Future deficit and debt figures are projections; the parties' statements on responsibility are political positions and are not judged here.

records.title_en: Coalition of the Willing's first major military exercise begins in Poland
records.summary_en:
Notes from Poland reports that thousands of troops from 11 countries began the KOALICJA exercise in Poland on 9 November, the Coalition of the Willing's first major drill, running until 22 November at Nowa Dęba about 100 km from the Ukrainian border and led by France and the UK through the Multinational Force-Ukraine. Around 2,800 coalition personnel take part, and with almost 2,000 Polish soldiers the total is nearly 5,000, covering land, air and sea operations.

The exercise prepares for supporting Ukraine after a possible peace deal; Poland says it will not send troops into Ukraine, and Russia's condemnation is a diplomatic statement.

records.title_en: Erasmus+ available again at all Hungarian universities
records.summary_en:
Telex reports that on 13 October the EU Council unanimously ended the rule-of-law conditionality procedure launched against Hungary in 2022, which had excluded public-interest asset management foundations and the universities they run from new EU funding commitments; the affected institutions' Erasmus+ grant agreements lapsed in 2024. The Tempus Public Foundation, which runs the programme, says all legal obstacles have been removed and all grant agreements signed, with regular student exchanges expected to resume in the second semester of 2026/2027.

The report's figures for lost funds are inconsistent and are not used; the time needed for full reintegration into EU funding is an interviewee's estimate.

records.title_en: Czechia and Hungary hold their first joint government meeting in Prague
records.summary_en:
Telex reports that Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar, with eight ministers, and Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš held the first Czech-Hungarian intergovernmental meeting in Prague, covering a high-speed rail line linking the Visegrád Four, energy cooperation, migration, EU competitiveness, the EU budget and enlargement. They signed a memorandum of understanding on joint transport projects, including rail investment and a Budapest–Prague line they hope to fund with EU money, and agreed to keep supporting energy companies and facilitate mutual investment; the next meeting is planned for Budapest in spring.

The memorandum is not a binding investment decision; Magyar's travel-time figures describe a project idea.

records.title_en: Hungarian government submits the 2027 budget bill to parliament
records.summary_en:
Telex reports that the Hungarian government submitted its 2027 budget bill to parliament late on 30 October. It plans central government spending of HUF 47,587 billion (HUF 49,025 billion in 2026), revenue of HUF 42,484 billion and a deficit of HUF 5,102 billion; the deficit falls from 7.5% of GDP in the amended 2026 budget to 4.9%, and government debt from 77.5% of GDP at the end of 2026 to 77.2% at the end of 2027. The bill assumes 2.4% GDP growth and 3% consumer price inflation in 2027.

The bill has been submitted but not voted on; the growth, inflation, deficit and debt figures are government projections.

records.title_en: Hungary's wind tender draws about 2,300 MW of bids for roughly 700 MW of grid capacity
records.summary_en:
Telex reports that Hungary's energy regulator MEKH launched a tender for new and expanded wind capacity in late August, with a 30 October deadline and earliest grid connection on 30 September 2030. Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány announced that 46 applications from 37 developers offered nearly 2,300 MW of new wind capacity, while the first round can connect only about 700 MW; applicants also committed to nearly 2,000 MWh of battery storage. The applications are being evaluated, with first results expected in mid-December.

These are tender applications, not awards; the minister's criticism of the previous government is a political statement.

records.title_en: Hungary's industrial output rises 8.2% year on year in September
records.summary_en:
Telex, citing the Hungarian Central Statistical Office's (KSH) first estimate, reports that industrial output in September 2026 rose 8.2% year on year, also 8.2% after working-day adjustment, and 0.9% month on month; August was up 8.8% on the year and 1.1% on the month, making two consecutive months above 8%. Output in January–September was 4.0% higher than a year earlier, with growth in vehicles, computer, electronic and optical products and electrical equipment, and a decline in food, drink and tobacco.

This is a first estimate and may be revised; the minister's description of industry "driving the economy" is his assessment.

records.title_en: Hungarian state secretary publishes more of the former government's letter of intent with CATL
records.summary_en:
Telex reports that Zsolt Tárkányi, a state secretary at the Ministry of Transport and Investment, published further pages of the 2022 letter of intent between Hungary's former government and Chinese battery maker CATL for its Debrecen plant. The letter provides for priority processing of visas and work permits for CATL and supplier staff, thousands of rental flats for workers to be built by the municipality with the state, help in obtaining land options beyond the initial site, and support such as innovation, training and energy-efficiency tax incentives.

The letter is non-binding and required further contracts and approvals; whether the workforce forecasts were met or the support was granted is not verified in the report.

records.title_en: Hungarian government ends its farm-machinery subsidy programme for Republika Srpska
records.summary_en:
Telex, citing Radio Free Europe, reports that the Hungarian government has ended a programme helping farmers in Bosnia's Republika Srpska buy Hungarian-made farm machinery. It was part of a €100 million aid package announced in 2022 by then-Prime Minister Viktor Orbán and Bosnian Serb leader Milorad Dodik, required farmers to pay at least 30% themselves and was administered for the government by the Budapest-based Central European Economic Development Network.

Neither the government nor the administrator explained the termination, and the fate of remaining funds is unknown; the report does not say who took the decision.

records.title_en: OTP and other banks challenge Hungary's mortgage rate cap at the Constitutional Court
records.summary_en:
Telex reports that OTP Bank, OTP Mortgage Bank and other market participants asked Hungary's Constitutional Court to review the statutory provision keeping the cap on variable residential mortgage rates in place indefinitely; OTP disclosed the filings in stock exchange notices on 6 November. The cap was introduced by the previous government by emergency decree in January 2022, lost its expiry date in April 2026 and was made ordinary law by the new parliament in May; it holds the reference rate at its 27 October 2021 level, with banks bearing the difference. At the end of 2025 it covered 218,000 contracts worth HUF 842 billion.

The petition is pending and the cap remains in force; the banks' and the government's views on its constitutionality and effects are their own positions.

records.title_en: Hungarian government to launch a HUF 25 billion export market-building programme
records.summary_en:
Telex reports that on 7 November Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány announced on social media that the government will launch a HUF 25 billion Market-Building Export Programme in 2027 to help more Hungarian companies sell their own products, brands and services abroad and strengthen SMEs' place in international value chains; the Széchenyi Card Programme continues, with HUF 250 billion budgeted for loan interest and fee subsidies in 2027.

This is an announced programme; the report gives no allocation method, eligibility rules or exact start date.

records.title_en: Hungarian government moves to close its railcar contract with Egypt
records.summary_en:
Telex reports that the Hungarian government plans to close the long-disputed 2018 railcar deal with Egypt by having the Dunakeszi works build 44 more cars for delivery by October 2027, as announced by Prime Minister Péter Magyar. Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy negotiated the terms with Egypt and says Egypt will pay for the 31 cars already delivered; Hungary's Eximbank reportedly extends its roughly €1 billion loan by a year to cover the remaining 44 cars.

The full terms are not public and the Eximbank extension comes from the report's sources; the Dunakeszi plant's future remains unclear.

records.title_en: Hungary's inflation rises to 2.0% in October
records.summary_en:
Telex, citing the Hungarian Central Statistical Office (KSH), reports that consumer prices in October 2026 rose 2.0% year on year and 0.4% month on month, the highest annual rate since April. Food prices fell 1.1% on the year, services rose 5.2%, spirits and tobacco 3.2% and durable goods 1.4%.

The report's annual figure for household energy conflicts with the finance ministry's account and is not used; analysts' views on monetary policy and the retail association's call to lift the margin cap are their own opinions.

records.title_en: Czech government extends fuel price regulation until 30 November
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International reports that after the government meeting on 26 October Finance Minister Alena Schillerová announced that fuel price regulation will be extended until 30 November. The measures in force since 1 October include government-set maximum prices for petrol and diesel, a cap on filling-station margins of CZK 2.50 per litre and a cut in diesel excise duty of CZK 2.35 per litre; similar regulation applied from early April to mid-July this year.

That the diesel tax cut is the largest EU law allows is the minister's statement; the report does not give the legal basis.

records.title_en: Czech transport ministry plans higher truck tolls from mid-2027
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International, citing the Czech News Agency, reports that the Ministry of Transport plans to raise tolls for trucks over 3.5 tonnes from mid-2027; for the most common category, trucks over 12 tonnes, per-kilometre rates would rise 18.5% on motorways and 26.6% on Class I roads. The ministry says the aim is to bring Czech heavy-truck tolls into line with neighbouring countries.

This is a ministry plan that has not been approved or implemented; the report gives no revenue estimate.

records.title_en: Czech opposition to challenge a law curbing the president's powers at the Constitutional Court
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International reports that the Czech opposition plans to challenge at the Constitutional Court a law passed by the ruling coalition that reduces the president's powers. The amendment moves the power to appoint and dismiss heads of permanent missions to international organisations such as NATO and the UN from the president to the foreign minister; President Petr Pavel vetoed it, but the coalition majority in the lower house overrode the veto. The motion has the support of 53 MPs and 38 senators.

The report does not say whether the motion has been filed; the opposition's view that the law is unconstitutional is its position, and there is no court ruling.

records.title_en: Babiš proposes voluntary licence fees for public broadcasters without direct state-budget funding
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International reports that Prime Minister Andrej Babiš said on TV Nova that the government is preparing a new funding model for Czech Television and Czech Radio that keeps licence fees voluntary and avoids "direct financing from the state budget", with the finance ministry drafting a proposal that would guarantee both broadcasters a certain amount. The bill passed its first reading the previous weekend amid public protests and returns for a second reading in January.

This is a proposal still being drafted, not an adopted law; the coalition was due to discuss the revised proposal the following Monday.

records.title_en: Czech central bank raises its key rate to 4% and cuts growth forecasts
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International reports that on 5 November the Czech National Bank raised its key interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 4%, the highest since early 2025. It cut its GDP growth forecast for 2026 from 2.2% in August to 1.7% and for 2027 from 2.7% to 2.5%, and expects average inflation of 2.1% in 2026 rising to 3.2% in 2027, well above earlier forecasts.

The growth and inflation figures are central bank forecasts; the report gives neither the vote split nor the effective date.

records.title_en: Czech retail sales growth slows to 4.1% in September
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International, citing the Czech Statistical Office, reports that retail sales in September 2026 rose 4.1% year on year, down from a revised 4.4% in August, the second consecutive slowdown, and 0.1% month on month. Non-food sales rose 7.3%, food 2.7% and online retail 14.5%, while fuel fell 4.5%.

The report does not say whether the figures are adjusted; no cause of the slowdown is inferred.

records.title_en: Czech lower house passes the Digital Economy Act implementing the EU Digital Services Act
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International reports that the Czech Chamber of Deputies approved the Digital Economy Act, setting stricter rules for online marketplaces and social networks and aligning Czech law with the EU Digital Services Act; it covers online intermediary services such as internet access, cloud services, search engines and web hosting, and strengthens child protection online. The bill was submitted by the previous Fiala government but not passed before last year's election; Czechia faces EU Court of Justice proceedings for late implementation.

Approval by the lower house does not mean the law is in force; the report gives neither the vote nor the remaining Senate and presidential steps.

records.title_en: Czech government approves an artificial intelligence council chaired by the prime minister
records.summary_en:
Radio Prague International reports that the Czech government approved a council to coordinate national AI policy, chaired by Prime Minister Andrej Babiš and including officials, researchers and business representatives, with priorities of introducing AI in public administration, supporting businesses and implementing the national AI strategy. The government also approved legislation setting oversight responsibilities and a regulatory framework for testing new AI technologies, with the Czech Telecommunications Office as the main supervisor.

The report gives no start date; the legislation still has to pass parliament.

records.title_en: Slovak regional elections: all eight regions re-elect their incumbent governors
records.summary_en:
TASR reports that Slovakia held municipal and regional elections on 24 October for four-year terms, and the State Electoral Commission confirmed the results on 25 October with turnout of 46.56%. All eight self-governing regions re-elected their incumbent governors: Juraj Droba in Bratislava with about 71%, Rastislav Trnka in Košice with about 32%, Milan Majerský in Prešov with over 48%, Branislav Bečík in Nitra with 51%, Erika Jurinová in Žilina with about 52%, Ondrej Lunter in Banská Bystrica with about 65%, Jozef Viskupič in Trnava with about 54% and Jaroslav Baška in Trenčín with about 57%.

These are results confirmed by the State Electoral Commission; no national political trend is inferred from local elections.

records.title_en: Slovak opposition says the coalition has lost its majority after an MP switches party
records.summary_en:
TASR reports that independent MP Roman Malatinec announced he is leaving the extra-parliamentary Rural Party led by Tourism and Sports Minister Rudolf Huliak to join a new party founded by former environment minister Tomáš Taraba, prompting the opposition to say Prime Minister Robert Fico's coalition has lost its majority. A majority requires 76 votes, and Freedom and Solidarity says the coalition now has 75; the coalition postponed this week's parliamentary votes to next week, and opposition parties including Progressive Slovakia called for an early election.

Whether the coalition still has 76 votes depends on talks; the opposition's claim is unverified, and Huliak says the coalition is not losing an MP.

records.title_en: Visegrád Four presidents adopt a joint declaration in Trenčín
records.summary_en:
TASR reports that the presidents of the Visegrád Four met at Trenčín Castle in Slovakia on 5 November in an expanded format with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen; Slovak President Peter Pellegrini hosted Czech President Petr Pavel, Polish President Karol Nawrocki and Hungarian head of state András Baka. They adopted a joint declaration backing a merit-based EU enlargement policy and Ukraine's sovereignty, territorial integrity and right to self-defence, and calling affordable, secure energy key to European competitiveness, with investment in energy infrastructure, storage and diverse sources including nuclear.

The declaration is a political statement, not a binding agreement; its content was provided by the Slovak President's Office.

records.title_en: Slovakia and Ukraine hold their fourth joint government session
records.summary_en:
TASR reports that the Slovak and Ukrainian governments held their fourth joint session in Lviv and Bratislava on 5 November with Prime Ministers Robert Fico and Serhii Koretskyi. They discussed humanitarian aid for Ukraine, including financial help to buy generators, post-war cooperation on electricity interconnectors and major transport projects such as a motorway link, and Ukraine's EU ambitions; the session was expected to produce a resolution setting tasks and deadlines for ministers.

No signed agreement was reported; the resolution and a joint business forum are plans, and gas transit was not mentioned.

records.title_en: Slovak soldiers and their families can now travel free by rail
records.summary_en:
TASR reports that under an agreement between the Defence Ministry and national passenger carrier ZSSK, announced on 9 November by Defence Minister Robert Kaliňák and Transport Minister Jozef Ráž, members of the Slovak Armed Forces, their immediate family and National Defence Forces volunteers and reservists can travel free in second class for commuting and family visits. ZSSK's director general said the benefit is "already practically in place", with travel passes still being finalised.

The report gives no start date and does not say who bears the cost; the ministers' claims about safety and environmental benefits come without data.

records.title_en: European Commission again leaves Slovakia off the migration solidarity exemption list
records.summary_en:
Radio Slovakia International reports that in its second annual migration report the European Commission did not list Slovakia among member states eligible for exemptions from contributing to the migration solidarity mechanism, naming Cyprus, Greece, Spain and Italy as qualifying for support in 2027 because of migration pressure. Slovakia had requested an exemption for 2026, citing the many Ukrainian refugees it hosts, and asked the Commission to reconsider; Prime Minister Robert Fico said in June that Slovakia would pay more than €4 million in 2026 instead of accepting over 200 migrants, but the payment has not been confirmed.

The 2027 arrangements still need approval by a qualified majority of member states; the figures on falling irregular crossings come from the Commission's report.

records.title_en: Slovak Foreign Minister Blanár holds talks with Wang Yi in Beijing
records.summary_en:
Radio Slovakia International, citing TASR, reports that Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanár met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing to discuss deepening the strategic partnership, improving trade and cooperation on emerging technologies. According to the Slovak foreign ministry, the talks covered Slovakia's bid for a non-permanent UN Security Council seat, easier access for Slovak firms to the Chinese market and cooperation in science, AI, robotics, advanced materials and green technology; Blanár called China Slovakia's largest trading partner outside Europe and urged more balanced trade.

No agreement signed in Beijing was reported; extending visa-free travel for Slovak citizens is an interest Slovakia expressed, not an agreed outcome.

records.title_en: At a joint Slovak-Czech government session, Fico calls Merz's EU-budget letter blackmail
records.summary_en:
TASR reports that, according to the Financial Times, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz wrote to European Council President António Costa threatening to block approval of the EU's 2028–2034 budget unless all member states commit to funding Ukraine from 2027. At a joint Slovak-Czech government session in Bratislava, Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico called this blackmail, rejected it and said he would discuss a response with Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš, who also rejected the threat; the issue is due at an informal EU leaders' meeting in Dublin on 12–13 November.

The letter's content comes from the Financial Times report; figures such as Ukraine's expected budget gap of about €70 billion next year are given without a source.

records.title_en: German GDP up 0.2% quarter on quarter in the third quarter
records.summary_en:
Germany's Federal Statistical Office published its first estimate on 30 October: GDP in the third quarter of 2026 rose 0.2% on the previous quarter after price, seasonal and calendar adjustment, and 1.3% year on year price-adjusted (1.2% also calendar-adjusted). Final consumption expenditure rose slightly, capital formation fell, and export growth, very strong in the first half, slowed noticeably; a review of earlier quarters left published quarterly growth rates unchanged.

This is a first estimate; detailed results follow on 25 November.

records.title_en: German inflation expected at 2.8% in October
records.summary_en:
Germany's Federal Statistical Office published provisional data on 30 October: consumer prices in October 2026 rose 2.8% year on year (3.3% in September) and fell 0.2% month on month; the harmonised index also rose 2.8%. Energy prices were up 12.2% (14.9% in September), food 0.4%, and core inflation excluding food and energy 2.1% (2.4% in September).

The data are provisional, with final results due on 11 November; the release gives no causes for the price changes.

records.title_en: German registered unemployment falls to 2.955 million in October
records.summary_en:
Germany's Federal Employment Agency reported on 30 October that registered unemployment in October 2026 was 2,955,000, down 40,000 on the month and up 44,000 on the year, for a rate of 6.3%; seasonally adjusted, unemployment rose by 4,000. Job vacancies reported to the agency were 654,000, up 31,000 on the year, and 98,000 people received short-time work benefit in August (preliminary).

Agency head Andrea Nahles's view that economic conditions are still insufficient for improvement is her assessment; no labour-market forecast is made here.

records.title_en: Auto supplier Schaeffler announces the closure of four German sites
records.summary_en:
ZDFheute, citing dpa and AFP, reports that on 3 November auto and industrial supplier Schaeffler announced a further cost-cutting programme eliminating 3,460 jobs in Europe and eventually closing five sites; in Germany 2,660 jobs and four sites (Dortmund, Morbach, Berlin and Schwalbach) are affected, with the cuts to be completed by 2028. The company plans €480 million in one-off costs and expects annual savings of €300 million from 2030, citing the difficult automotive environment and a slower ramp-up of electric vehicles.

These are announced company plans; job figures in the report are not fully consistent, and the company's figures are used here.

records.title_en: German coalition enters final negotiations on the 2027 federal budget
records.summary_en:
ZDFheute, citing Reuters, reports that the CDU/CSU-SPD coalition is finalising the draft 2027 federal budget, with the Bundestag budget committee's concluding session starting on Thursday. The core budget plans €555.4 billion in spending and €118.7 billion in new borrowing, or €203.7 billion including the special funds for the Bundeswehr and infrastructure; disputes include a planned plastic tax and sugar tax, the Union's call for electricity tax cuts and the SPD's insistence on keeping housing benefit.

This is a draft budget still under negotiation, not adopted; the finance ministry's estimates of funding gaps for 2028–2030 are calculations.

records.title_en: COP31 opens without German Chancellor Merz
records.summary_en:
ZDFheute reports that the UN climate conference COP31 runs for two weeks from 9 November in Antalya, Turkey, with nearly 200 states and about 70 heads of state or government expected. Chancellor Friedrich Merz will not attend, with a government spokesperson saying only that his schedule is very full; the environment minister and technical negotiators will travel to Antalya. Germany pledged €6 billion a year from its budget for climate protection and adaptation in the Global South and has reached €4.7 billion.

Speculation in the report about the reasons for his absence and the criticism voiced are commentary and are not judged here.

records.title_en: German gas storage operators warn of possible shortfalls in extreme cold
records.summary_en:
ZDFheute reports that INES, the association representing more than 90% of German gas storage capacity, says German storage was about 61% full on 1 November, short of the legal 80% target most facilities had to meet by that date. INES calculates that in an extremely cold winter like 2010 up to 6.6 TWh of gas could be missing in each of January–March 2027, and calls for a state gas reserve or injection incentives; Economy Minister Katherina Reiche rejects state intervention and says winter supply is secure, and the Federal Network Agency rates the risk of tight supply as low.

The 6.6 TWh figure is an INES model result for an extreme scenario, not a forecast; under normal or mild temperatures INES also considers supply secure.

records.title_en: CDU nominates Ilse Aigner as candidate for federal president
records.summary_en:
ZDFheute, citing AFP, reports that the CDU federal executive, on the proposal of party leader and Chancellor Friedrich Merz, nominated CSU politician Ilse Aigner as candidate for federal president, to be elected by the Federal Convention on 30 January 2027. Aigner was originally proposed by Markus Söder; the CDU/CSU and SPD hold a majority among the convention's 1,260 members, and Aigner may also receive some Green votes. Merz rejected criticism that the process had been bumpy.

This is a party nomination, not an election result; no outcome of the Federal Convention vote is predicted.

records.title_en: Austria's coalition agrees a social assistance reform
records.summary_en:
ORF reports that the ÖVP-SPÖ-NEOS coalition agreed a reform of social assistance (Sozialhilfe Neu): fixed amounts replace the current maximum rates in the federal framework law, with a basic monthly amount of €1,016 for recipients able to work and €861 for recognised refugees; full benefits require proof of integration efforts, and sanctions can cut benefits by at least 25% or remove them. Rates are uniform for the first child and from the fifth child, while states set rates for children two to four within a federal range.

The draft goes to public consultation on Friday, with a National Council vote targeted for November and entry into force on 1 January 2027; it is not yet law, and the criticism and support quoted are the parties' positions.

records.title_en: WIFO flash estimate: Austria's economy grew 0.2% quarter on quarter in the third quarter
records.summary_en:
trend., citing the Austrian Institute of Economic Research (WIFO) flash estimate, reports that Austria's real GDP grew 0.2% quarter on quarter in the third quarter after a decline in the second, and 0.6% year on year. Foreign trade and investment made slight positive contributions, industry was subdued, construction stayed weak and most services performed well.

This is a flash estimate and may be revised; no further economic path is inferred.

records.title_en: Austria extends its fuel price brake to 30 November
records.summary_en:
news.at, citing a finance ministry press release of 30 October, reports that Austria's fuel price relief is extended by one month to 30 November 2026: an amendment to the Mineral Oil Tax Act cuts the tax by 6.7 cents per litre, and a federal government regulation requires large suppliers to cut margins by 3.5 cents per litre, for total relief of about 12 cents per litre including VAT. The margin cap covers diesel B7 and Eurosuper E10 at vertically integrated oil companies and operators with more than 30 stations; lost tax revenue for October is estimated at about €55 million, shared by the federal government, states and municipalities.

The government's estimate that a 10-cent fall in fuel prices lowers inflation by about 0.2 points is its own; the parties' assessments are their positions.

records.title_en: Austrian parliamentary budget office: 2026 deficit projected at 4.1% of GDP
records.summary_en:
On 2 November the Austrian Parliament's budget office published its analysis of the finance ministry's 14 October report on effective measures to correct the excessive deficit. Under its autumn projection, Austria's Maastricht deficit is €22.0 billion or 4.1% of GDP in 2026 and €20.1 billion or 3.6% in 2027, while government debt rises from 80.7% of GDP in 2025 to 82.4% in 2026 and 83.2% in 2027. The report is submitted to the European Commission and Council under the excessive deficit procedure and reflects WIFO's October forecast and budget execution.

The 2026 and 2027 figures are projections; no judgement on the EU procedure is made here.

records.title_en: Austrian unemployment and training numbers rise year on year for the 43rd month in October
records.summary_en:
ORF reports that at the end of October 2026, 389,941 people were registered with the AMS as unemployed or in training, 1,823 (0.5%) more than a year earlier, the 43rd consecutive annual increase. Unemployment among women rose 3.8% while among men it fell 2.6%, and among people over 50 it rose 4.4%. Vienna and Carinthia saw declines and the other states increases, led by Lower Austria (+5.2%) and Styria (+4.5%); immediately available vacancies fell 3.4% to about 73,800.

The bonus-malus model for employers put forward by labour and union bodies is a proposal, and the views quoted are the parties' positions.

records.title_en: Statistics Austria flash estimate: October inflation unchanged at 3.6%
records.summary_en:
trend. reports that Statistics Austria's flash estimate published on 4 November put October 2026 inflation at 3.6%, unchanged from September; the harmonised index, used for euro-area comparison, was 3.5% (3.6% in September), with prices up 0.3% on the month. Energy rose 16.5% year on year and services 4.1%, the main driver; food, tobacco and alcohol were unchanged and industrial goods rose 0.9%.

This is a flash estimate, with final data to follow; the parties' views on prices and policy are their own positions.

records.title_en: Austrian rail collective agreement talks progress without a deal
records.summary_en:
ORF reports that collective bargaining for about 55,000 rail employees at 98 companies entered its fourth round, and for the first time both sides have a joint calculation and monetary valuation of reduced working hours. The unions want a 38.5-hour week for everyone now working 40 hours, with pay demands of 3.26% to 3.9% depending on conditions; employers want the originally planned two-year agreement as the basis, saying shorter hours are only feasible in that structure.

No agreement has been reached, and no outcome of the talks is predicted.

records.title_en: voestalpine's half-year profit after tax rises 46% as it lowers its full-year outlook
records.summary_en:
ORF Upper Austria reports that voestalpine's profit after tax in the first half of the 2026/27 financial year rose 46% to €290 million, about €100 million of it from one-off effects; revenue was almost unchanged at €7.7 billion and EBITDA rose 17% to €846 million. The company lowered its full-year EBITDA forecast from up to €1.85 billion to €1.6–1.7 billion, citing higher energy and logistics costs from the Middle East war; the workforce fell 2% to 48,619, and about 150 production jobs will go at the Kindberg site by March 2027.

The full-year outlook and the effects of the green steel project are forward-looking company statements, not realised results.

records.title_en: Negotiations on Austria's military service reform continue after consultation
records.summary_en:
ORF reports that public consultation on the government's draft military service reform closes the next day, with the Greens meeting the governing parties the day after; some parts need a two-thirds majority, and whether the Greens will provide it is unclear. The Freedom Party left the talks about a month earlier, demanding that civilian service be extended at the same time, whereas the draft extends it only if too few volunteer for military service; the Greens want no financial disadvantage for civilian servants and reject a quota for the Voluntary Social Year.

Negotiations are ongoing and the draft has not been adopted; no vote outcome is predicted.

records.title_en: Romania's new Prime Minister Niculescu makes his first visit to Chișinău
records.summary_en:
Radio Romania International reports that Prime Minister Luca Niculescu, in office for a week, made his first foreign visit to Chișinău, as is customary, and after meeting Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan said the two countries would speed up joint infrastructure and energy projects and strengthen economic ties. Romania pledged support for Moldova's European integration, security and energy independence and backs opening the last two negotiating clusters of Moldova's EU accession by the end of the year; they also discussed electricity interconnection and the possibility of Moldova receiving gas from the Black Sea Neptun Deep field from next heating season.

No formal agreement was reported; Neptun Deep gas supplies were only discussed as a possibility.

records.title_en: Romanian, Bulgarian and Turkish defence ministers discuss Black Sea shipping security in Sofia
records.summary_en:
Radio Romania International reports that Defence Ministers Ștefan-Radu Oprea of Romania, Dimitar Stoyanov of Bulgaria and Yaşar Güler of Turkey met in Sofia on Wednesday to discuss protecting civilian shipping in the Black Sea. They agreed to improve maritime situational awareness, exchange more information and coordinate their navies more closely, and stressed continued work on the trilateral MCM Black Sea mine countermeasures initiative; Romania's minister called for NATO support for surveillance, early warning and counter-drone capabilities and better protection of critical infrastructure in Romania's exclusive economic zone.

No signed agreement or declaration was reported; counts of attacks on merchant ships are the report's and are not independently verified here.

records.title_en: Romania and Moldova sign a military partnership under the EU's SAFE programme
records.summary_en:
Radio Romania International reports that Romania and Moldova signed a military partnership under the EU's SAFE programme, which finances defence investment and encourages joint procurement, described as the first of its kind under SAFE. The two armies will jointly procure military vehicles made by Italy's IVECO in Petrești, Dâmbovița; Romania's defence minister said the Romanian army will receive nearly 3,000 of them, 62 of which are earmarked for Moldova.

The report gives no amounts or financing form; claims about investment and jobs are the prime minister's statements.

records.title_en: Romania's nine-month budget deficit falls to 3.81% of GDP
records.summary_en:
Radio Romania International, citing the Ministry of Finance, reports that Romania's budget deficit in the first nine months of 2026 was 3.81% of GDP, down from 5.31% a year earlier, or about €14.6 billion, roughly €4.5 billion less. Public investment rose about 30% to over €20 billion, more than 65% financed from EU funds. Finance Minister Alexandru Nazare said reaching the year-end target of 6.2% depends on receiving the final Recovery and Resilience Plan tranches of about €4 billion.

The 6.2% figure and next year's move towards 5% are targets, not outcomes; the report does not distinguish cash and ESA accounting.

records.title_en: Romanian prime minister tells foreign investors economic relaunch is the government's priority
records.summary_en:
Radio Romania International reports that on Wednesday Prime Minister Luca Niculescu told foreign investors in Romania that relaunching the economy is the new government's main goal, with curbing the deficit and inflation as complementary aims; he cited a first budget adjustment and said Romania raised €4.5 billion from financial institutions through a Eurobond issue. The report notes that foreign direct investment fell 62% year on year in the first eight months; Niculescu asked his chancellery to organise quarterly meetings between the government and investors.

Fighting tax evasion, cutting red tape and OECD accession are announced directions, not implemented measures; improved international credibility is the prime minister's view.

records.title_en: Romanian and Ukrainian foreign ministers hold talks in Bucharest
records.summary_en:
Radio Romania International reports that Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha met Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculăescu in Bucharest and held a joint press conference with Central European Initiative Secretary General Franco Dal Mas. Sybiha said Ukraine will uphold high standards for protecting minorities, including Romanians, and would look into reports of ethnic Romanian pupils unable to study in their mother tongue; Neculăescu said the joint intergovernmental committee on minorities should meet as soon as possible. They also discussed Black Sea security and Ukraine's European integration.

No agreement was reported signed; the statements on minority rights and freedom of navigation are the two sides' positions.

records.title_en: Romanian government considers diversifying energy sources and expanding storage
records.summary_en:
Radio Romania International reports that Prime Minister Luca Niculescu said at the Cernavodă nuclear plant over the weekend that the government is considering diversifying energy sources and building storage capacity to strengthen energy independence; the plant was shut in summer because of the Danube's low flow, forcing Romania to rely on imports in recent months. Energy Minister Dumitru Chisăliță proposed a register of vulnerable consumers to set aid amounts and said a fully deregulated market cannot be reached in a few months; the ministry is weighing extending compensation and subsidies to vulnerable household and non-household consumers.

These are considerations and proposals, not decisions; a detailed report on the energy mix is expected this week.

records.title_en: Von der Leyen visits Bucharest and announces €50 million for a Black Sea maritime security hub
records.summary_en:
Radio Romania International reports that European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Bucharest and discussed with President Nicușor Dan the Black Sea region's importance for world trade, European energy security and Ukraine's reconstruction. She announced €50 million in EU funding for a Black Sea Maritime Security Hub to be co-managed by Romania and Bulgaria, plus €10 million for search and rescue in the region, and also met Prime Minister Luca Niculescu.

These are announced funding commitments; statements about Russia's aims and freedom of navigation are the two sides' positions.
